stem: An Auto Loader stream ingests JSON files with cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode left at its default. A producer adds a new field to the payload. The team must predict what happens on the next micro-batch, and what they have to do to resume processing without editing the schema by hand.

option_texts.A: The stream fails once the new columns are added to the schema, then a restart resumes
option_texts.B: The stream keeps running and the new field is silently discarded from every record
option_texts.C: The stream keeps running and the new field is captured in the rescued data column
option_texts.D: The stream fails and the new columns are rejected, so the schema must be edited by hand

drill_answer_short: addNewColumns adds the column then fails the stream; restarting picks up the new schema
decision_hinge: With addNewColumns, the default mode, the stream fails with an UnknownFieldException after Auto Loader adds the new columns to the schema.

plausible_options.C: what they have to do to resume processing

B.requires_fact: The schemaLocation option enables schema inference and evolution, and Auto Loader adds the new columns to the schema rather than discarding them.

eliminated_by.D: without editing the schema by hand

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated — no evolution mode silently drops a newly seen field
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — that is the rescue mode behaviour, not the default
distractor_traps.D: T4: breaks a stated requirement — the stem rules out hand-editing the schema

stem: A streaming ingestion pipeline must never fail when a producer introduces an unexpected field, because the on-call rotation cannot absorb overnight restarts. The team still wants those unexpected fields retained somewhere so an analyst can inspect them the following morning rather than losing them.

option_texts.A: Set the evolution mode to addNewColumns so each unexpected field joins the schema
option_texts.B: Set the evolution mode to rescue so unexpected fields land in the rescued data column
option_texts.C: Set the evolution mode to none so the schema is fixed and unexpected fields are dropped
option_texts.D: Set the evolution mode to failOnNewColumns so the team is alerted to unexpected fields

drill_answer_short: rescue keeps the stream alive and puts unexpected fields in the rescued data column
decision_hinge: In the case of a mismatch, Auto Loader rescues the column by placing the data in the rescued data column.

plausible_options.C: must never fail when a producer introduces an unexpected field

A.signal: the on-call rotation cannot absorb overnight restarts
A.requires_fact: With addNewColumns the stream fails with an UnknownFieldException after Auto Loader adds the new columns to the schema.

eliminated_by.D: the on-call rotation cannot absorb overnight restarts

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling — it does capture the field, but it stops the stream to do it
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — a fixed schema also keeps the stream alive, but it drops the fields instead of retaining them
distractor_traps.D: T4: breaks a stated requirement — failing on new columns is exactly the overnight restart being avoided

stem: An engineer wants an Auto Loader stream to infer the schema of incoming JSON and to keep tracking how that schema changes over time. They are reviewing which single option has to be present for inference and evolution to be enabled at all, before tuning anything else about the behaviour.

option_texts.A: cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes, asking Auto Loader to pick specific column types
option_texts.B: cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode, selecting how schema changes should be handled
option_texts.C: cloudFiles.schemaLocation, giving Auto Loader a path to track schema changes
option_texts.D: mergeSchema, letting the Delta write accept a changed schema on each commit

drill_answer_short: The schemaLocation option is what enables schema inference and evolution
decision_hinge: The schemaLocation option enables schema inference and evolution, and Auto Loader uses schemaLocation to track schema changes to the input data over time.

plausible_options.B: keep tracking how that schema changes over time

eliminated_by.A: which single option has to be present for inference and evolution to be enabled

D.signal: to infer the schema of incoming JSON
D.requires_fact: Auto Loader uses the schemaLocation option to track schema changes to the input data over time on the read side.

distractor_traps.A: T8: scope error — type inference refines the inferred types rather than enabling inference
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — evolution mode shapes the behaviour but does not switch inference on
distractor_traps.D: T2: wrong layer — mergeSchema is a write-side Delta option, not an Auto Loader read option

stem: A team is standing up its first Auto Loader stream over a storage container receiving a moderate daily volume at irregular times. They want the simplest possible setup and have been told they may not provision any queue or notification services in the cloud account for this project.

option_texts.A: File notification mode, which leverages notification and queue services in the account
option_texts.B: A custom stream tracking processed file names in a side table the team maintains
option_texts.C: A scheduled COPY INTO statement rerun every minute against the storage container
option_texts.D: Directory listing mode, which identifies new files by listing the input directory

drill_answer_short: Directory listing is the default and needs no cloud notification or queue services
decision_hinge: Auto Loader uses directory listing mode by default, and in directory listing mode Auto Loader identifies new files by listing the input directory.

plausible_options.C: They want the simplest possible setup

eliminated_by.A: may not provision any queue or notification services in the cloud account

B.signal: receiving a moderate daily volume at irregular times
B.requires_fact: Auto Loader supports two modes for detecting new files, directory listing and file notification, and uses directory listing mode by default.

distractor_traps.A: T4: breaks a stated requirement — this mode needs exactly the cloud services the team may not provision
distractor_traps.B: T7: over-engineering — Auto Loader already tracks processed files without a hand-built side table
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — COPY INTO is a real idempotent loader, but polling it every minute is not the simplest setup

stem: A container has accumulated millions of objects and now receives a hundred thousand new files a day. The existing Auto Loader stream has grown slow and the cloud bill is dominated by storage list operations. The team can provision cloud services and wants new files detected without repeatedly enumerating the directory.

option_texts.A: Switch to file notification mode, which uses notification and queue services
option_texts.B: Keep directory listing mode but shorten the interval between listing passes
option_texts.C: Keep directory listing mode and raise the cluster size so listing finishes faster
option_texts.D: Replace the stream with COPY INTO, which skips loaded files without cloud services

drill_answer_short: File notification mode detects files via cloud notifications instead of listing
decision_hinge: File notification mode leverages file notification and queue services in your cloud infrastructure account, rather than identifying new files by listing the input directory.

plausible_options.D: receives a hundred thousand new files a day

eliminated_by.B: wants new files detected without repeatedly enumerating the directory

C.signal: the cloud bill is dominated by storage list operations
C.requires_fact: In directory listing mode Auto Loader identifies new files by listing the input directory, so the number of list operations does not fall with more compute.

distractor_traps.B: T4: breaks a stated requirement — more frequent listing is more enumeration, not less
distractor_traps.C: T5: right diagnosis, wrong symptom — the bottleneck is storage API calls, not cluster capacity
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling — COPY INTO is genuinely idempotent, but it still discovers files by listing them

stem: A failed pipeline run left a target table holding partial results from a set of CSV files loaded with COPY INTO. The team has corrected the transformation and now needs every file in the source location processed again, including the ones COPY INTO already recorded as loaded on the earlier run.

option_texts.A: Add COPY_OPTIONS with mergeSchema set to true so the load is repeated
option_texts.B: Add COPY_OPTIONS with force set to true so loaded files are read again
option_texts.C: Add FORMAT_OPTIONS with modifiedAfter so older files are included again
option_texts.D: Drop and recreate the target table so COPY INTO forgets what it loaded

drill_answer_short: force defaults to false; setting it true reloads files already recorded as loaded
decision_hinge: COPY INTO is a retryable and idempotent operation, files in the source location that have already been loaded are skipped, and force is a boolean option defaulting to false.

plausible_options.D: needs every file in the source location processed again

A.signal: The team has corrected the transformation
A.requires_fact: Files in the source location that have already been loaded are skipped by COPY INTO unless force is set.

eliminated_by.C: including the ones COPY INTO already recorded as loaded on the earlier run

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling — a real COPY INTO option, but one that governs schema rather than reload behaviour
distractor_traps.C: T8: scope error — a modification-time filter narrows which files are considered, it does not clear the loaded record
distractor_traps.D: T7: over-engineering — destroying the table to reset bookkeeping when an option already exists for it

stem: A nightly SQL job runs the same COPY INTO statement against a cloud storage location that accumulates files through the day. An auditor asks what stops yesterday's files being counted twice when the identical statement runs again tonight against that same location.

option_texts.A: COPY INTO compares every row against the target and merges on a primary key
option_texts.B: COPY INTO truncates the target table before loading that same location again
option_texts.C: COPY INTO skips files in the source location that have already been loaded
option_texts.D: COPY INTO requires a modifiedAfter filter, without which the statement is rejected

drill_answer_short: COPY INTO is idempotent — already-loaded files in the source location are skipped
decision_hinge: COPY INTO is a retryable and idempotent operation, and files in the source location that have already been loaded are skipped.

plausible_options.A: what stops yesterday's files being counted twice

eliminated_by.B: a cloud storage location that accumulates files through the day

D.signal: runs the same COPY INTO statement against a cloud storage location
D.requires_fact: COPY INTO is a retryable and idempotent operation that skips files already loaded, without requiring an additional filter.

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling — row-level deduplication is a real pattern, but it belongs to MERGE rather than COPY INTO
distractor_traps.B: T4: breaks a stated requirement — truncating would discard the accumulated history the job is building
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — no modification-time filter is required for the statement to run

stem: A JSON file has been uploaded to a volume named source_files, which lives in the schema events inside the catalog analytics. An engineer wants to query that file directly from SQL and has to write the governed path to it correctly on the first attempt.
decision_hinge: Unity Catalog volumes are accessed through a path of the form /Volumes/catalog name/schema name/volume name, following the same three-level namespace as tables.

plausible_options.B: has to write the governed path to it correctly on the first attempt

eliminated_by.A: An engineer wants to query that file directly from SQL

C.signal: a volume named source_files, which lives in the schema events inside the catalog analytics
C.requires_fact: A volume path places the catalog name first, then the schema name, then the volume name.

distractor_traps.A: T6: stale behaviour — the legacy DBFS root path predates governed volumes
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — the right three names in the path, ordered backwards
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — catalog and schema transposed in an otherwise correct path

stem: A team must consume clickstream events from a topic on a remote broker and begin reading only from the newest offsets rather than replaying history. They are writing the reader now and need the option names that identify the broker, name the topic, and set the starting position.

option_texts.A: format kafka, with kafka.bootstrap.servers, subscribe, and startingOffsets
option_texts.B: format kafka, with kafka.broker.list, topic.name, and offset.reset.policy
option_texts.C: format cloudFiles, with cloudFiles.format kafka and cloudFiles.subscribe
option_texts.D: a readStream.kafka helper taking the broker, the topic, and the offset order

drill_answer_short: kafka.bootstrap.servers, subscribe and startingOffsets configure the Kafka reader
decision_hinge: Databricks reads Kafka with format kafka, using kafka.bootstrap.servers for the broker, subscribe for the topic, and startingOffsets to set where reading begins.

plausible_options.B: need the option names that identify the broker, name the topic, and set the starting position

C.signal: consume clickstream events from a topic on a remote broker
C.requires_fact: Databricks connects to Apache Kafka using the kafka format with the kafka.bootstrap.servers and subscribe options.

eliminated_by.D: They are writing the reader now

distractor_traps.B: T6: stale behaviour — broker.list style names belong to an older Kafka client, not the current Spark reader options
distractor_traps.C: T2: wrong layer — cloudFiles is the Auto Loader source for cloud object storage, not for a broker
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — there is no readStream.kafka positional helper on the reader

stem: An engineer assumes a streaming table can read continuously from a relational database over a plain JDBC connection, the way one reads from a broker topic. They are about to design a near real-time pipeline on that assumption and want it checked before any code is written.

option_texts.A: The assumption holds, because a streaming table turns any connection into a stream
option_texts.B: The assumption fails, because a plain JDBC connection supports batch reads rather than streaming
option_texts.C: The assumption holds, because the database is polled on an interval and emits each changed row
option_texts.D: The assumption fails, because relational sources can only be read after an export to files

drill_answer_short: Plain JDBC is a batch source; continuous capture needs a managed connector instead
decision_hinge: Databricks queries external databases using JDBC through the JDBC data source, which reads a table or query as a batch rather than as a continuous stream.

plausible_options.C: They are about to design a near real-time pipeline on that assumption

A.signal: a streaming table can read continuously from a relational database
A.requires_fact: Databricks reads external databases with the JDBC data source, which loads a table or query rather than subscribing to changes.

eliminated_by.D: want it checked before any code is written

distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — polling is a real pattern, but it is not what a plain JDBC read does on its own
distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated — declaring a table streaming does not grant a batch source streaming semantics
distractor_traps.D: T8: scope error — an export is one workaround, not the reason the assumption fails
